title: Titanium Derailleur Hanger
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this frame hardware application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by rear derailleur hanger dropout interface and specific design requirements.
process: CNC turning Swiss-type for frame hardware geometry
Thread rolling DIN 13-1 6g with 0.5mm corner radius

surfaceTreatment: Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for rear derailleur hanger application
commonFailures: Thread galling Ti-on-Ti assembly - prevented by MoS2 anti-seize compound and -20% installation torque — critical for rear derailleur hanger performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Derailleur Hanger suitable for Rear derailleur hanger dropout interface?
faq.a: Titanium Derailleur Hanger uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address frame hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Derailleur Hanger?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Derailleur Hanger is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for rear derailleur hanger requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Derailleur Hanger require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. rear derailleur hanger components require Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water — tailored for rear derailleur hanger application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
